name: Specific Productivity Calculator (qP)
seoDesc: Specific productivity is the amount of product one cell makes per day, which is the only fair way to compare cell lines, media and processes of different size
summary:
Specific productivity is the amount of product one cell makes per day, which is the only fair way to compare cell lines, media and processes of different sizes. It returns specific productivity, total product per batch, volumetric productivity and days needed for the target titre, and the panel shows all of them at once.

This calculator derives qP from titre, cell density and culture time, then projects the titre a longer run would give. Every result is derived from the boxes you fill in, so changing one input updates the whole panel at once. Units are stated on every box and in every result, so a figure copied out of a protocol, a datasheet or a chart can be entered without converting it first.

sections.title: The formula behind the Specific Productivity (qP)
sections.html:
qP = titre ÷ (VCD × days) × 1000 [pg/cell/day], with VCD in 10⁶ cells/mL

The symbols in the formula
SymbolWhat it stands forUnit
titreproduct concentration at harvestg/L
VCDtime-weighted mean viable cell density10⁶/mL
tduration of the production phasedays

sections.title: How do I use the Specific Productivity (qP)?
sections.html:
The form asks only for what the formula needs — nothing is optional decoration.

  1. Enter the values you already have. Every box accepts a decimal point and a minus sign; thousands separators are ignored.
  2. The grey boxes are results: they are worked out from your inputs and cannot be typed into.
  3. Press Calculate. The results fill in together, and from then on they follow every edit you make — there is no page to reload and nothing to submit.

sections.title: A worked example
sections.html:
Take the default values the page opens with: product titre of 2.5 g/L, viable cell density of 12 10⁶/mL, production phase of 10 days, working volume of 2,000 L, target titre of 4 g/L.

Substituting them into the formula gives specific productivity of 20.83 pg/cell/d, total product per batch of 5,000 g, volumetric productivity of 0.25 g/L/day, days needed for the target titre of 16 days.

The arithmetic is the page's own: change one box and the result moves by the amount the formula implies, which is the quickest way to convince yourself the tool is honest.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
A raw figure only means something next to the bands it is normally judged against. Here is the scale that goes with this one:

How to read the result
ResultBandWhat it means
1 – 10Lowunoptimised CHO pools
10 – 30Typicalstable CHO fed-batch processes
30 – 60Highoptimised hosts, strong promoters, good media
above 60Very highcheck the assay — this is unusual

  • Use the integral of viable cell concentration over time (IVCC) rather than a single VCD reading; a run that peaks at 20 × 10⁶ cells/mL for two days produces far less than one that holds 10 × 10⁶ for ten days.

  • qP is the fair comparison between a 2 L bioreactor and a 2 000 L tank, because titre alone rewards scale and harvest timing.

  • Volumetric productivity (g/L/day) is what capacity planning uses; specific productivity is what cell-line development optimises.

sections.title: What are the common mistakes?
sections.html:
The arithmetic is simple; the inputs are where things go wrong. The usual culprits:

  • Plugging in peak VCD instead of the time-weighted average, which understates qP badly.
  • Comparing qP across products with different molecular weights without converting to molar terms.
  • Ignoring the harvest/clarification losses between the bioreactor and the reported titre.

faq.q: What is a typical qP for CHO cells?
faq.a: Roughly 10–30 pg/cell/day in fed-batch, with high producers reaching 40–60.
Trapezoidal integration of viable cell density against time over the production phase; qP = product ÷ IVCC.

faq.q: What does the Specific Productivity (qP) actually calculate?
faq.a: It returns specific productivity, total product per batch, volumetric productivity and days needed for the target titre. Each one is derived by the formula on this page, so you can check any figure by hand.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — and if you change an input, every result updates with it.

faq.q: Why is the answer different from the one in my protocol?
faq.a: Nearly always a unit or a rounding difference. This calculator works in the units printed next to each box, keeps full precision internally and only rounds for display, so recomputing from the rounded numbers on screen can differ in the last digit.

faq.q: Can I use it with the numbers straight from a datasheet?
faq.a: Yes. Every box states its unit, and nothing is converted behind your back, so a figure copied from a datasheet, a kit insert or a protocol goes in as printed.
